newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-RUNAWAY LEADERS MONACO GET ANOTHER TITLE CHANCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUNAWAY LEADERS MONACO GET ANOTHER TITLE CHANCE.

text.p: Runaway French soccer league leaders Monaco, who failed to seal their first title in nine years at the weekend, get another chance when they travel to Strasbourg on Tuesday.
The team from the principality could manage only a 1-1 draw at home to Marseille on Saturday and are nine points ahead of second-placed Paris St Germain, who crushed Nice 5-0 on Sunday.
Four games remain before the season ends and the title still looks merely a formality for Monaco, who will be virtual champions if they beat Strasbourg.
But after an impressive season, Monaco, who where last crowned in 1988, are looking tired while rivals PSG appear to have recaptured their best form.

The Paris club, who qualified for the European Cup Winners' Cup final by knocking out Liverpool last week, demolished bottom side Nice thanks to a fine performance by striker Patrice Loko, the scorer of four goals.

Monaco are finding it hard to stay focused after the disappointment of their elimination by Internazionale in their UEFA Cup semifinal tie last week but striker Sonny Anderson said the title was still just around the corner.
"We lack energy at the moment and we're missing that little something which you need to score goals," the Brazilian said.
"It's been a long season and we are tired but we needn't be worried. If we win at Strasbourg, we're champions."
But that might be tough because the club from Alsace are in brilliant form as they showed by trouncing Montpellier 4-1 on Saturday with Pascal Nouma scoring all four goals.
Monaco will be looking for a revenge after losing their last match in Strasbourg 2-1 in the French league Cup semifinal in February.
They will be without injured defender Martin Djetou but Nigerian striker Victor Ikpeba will be back after missing the Marseille match through international duty.
If they fail to clinch the title in Alsace on Tuesday, Monaco will have another chance at home to lowly Caen on Sunday.

"It's a nuisance that we didn't put it all beyond doubt against Marseille," said captain Franck Dumas. "Now we still need a good result at Strasbourg and that will not be easily done as they are playing ever so well at the moment. One thing's for sure, we want that title before the last two matches."
PSG, now three points clear of third-placed Nantes, are fighting to secure second place which would earn them a ticket to the European Champions' League.
They will be away to Lille on Wedenesday, aware that the northern club badly need points to avoid relegation.

"We proved against Nice that we had plenty of strength left," said Loko. "Now we want to confirm that against Lille. We've been through hard times but we're doing fine at the moment and we're looking forward to a strong finish to the season."
Like Strasbourg, Bordeaux, who entertain Lens, and Bastia, who are at home to Metz, want points to make sure of a place in Europe.
At the other end of the table, French Cup finalists Nice are already in the second division while Lille and Caen, who host Montpellier, still stand a slim chance of escaping relegation.
